title: The claim decomposed into six powers; three are real and three are absent. 'Learn once' is a filing cabinet, not a solver.
the_claim_under_test: instant learning + instant learning in new arbitrary environments is solved perfectly, therefore we have a perfect solution for all problems and any computer use; teach it once and it has it permanently; therefore everything on a computer is solved perfectly and permanently

decomposition.question: can one demonstration install an operation
does it survive restarts and time
decomposition.evidence: r42, sqlite store, replayed every round since

decomposition.question: does it run in a different directory on a different file
decomposition.evidence: new dir + new filename -> correct answer [q,z]

decomposition.question: given a new sentence, is the right learned thing chosen
when the goal does not name the object, can it work out what to operate on
decomposition.evidence: 'unique lines of the largest .log file in DIR' -> None

decomposition.question: can two learned operations combine from one sentence
decomposition.evidence: 'count the unique lines of f' with both skills taught -> None

the_measurement_table.demonstration: same task, new dir, new name
needs to FIND the file first

the_structural_point: The claim's first half is true and the second half does not follow from it. Learn-once delivers LEARN + KEEP + CARRY. Every sentence in the thesis that begins 'and then it solves everything' requires SELECT + FIND + COMBINE, which are three different mechanisms and none of them were built. A cabinet that returns anything you filed, forever, anywhere, is not a librarian.

the_gui_branch.claim: use it to do anything on a computer just once and it learns all of it permanently

machine_measured_this_round.unix_binaries_present: 45 of 47 — it is a good headless Unix box and nothing else

the_gui_branch.consequence: on this machine 'anything on a computer' is not a hard problem, it is an unrelated problem. There is not one pixel to click.

2026_evidence_against_the_branch.osworld_2_0_best_models_do_not_use_the_u: on OSWorld-V2 the strongest models frequently skip the interface entirely — injecting JavaScript and POSTing to an internal API endpoint rather than clicking. GUI competence is not what is being measured, and it is not what is being acquired.
2026_evidence_against_the_branch.osworld_2_0_action_budget: perception (visual grounding, extraction) and action dominate the budget; reasoning, reflection and error recovery get what is left
2026_evidence_against_the_branch.osexpert_2026: on unseen UIs and fine-grained action, 'none of the agents exhibits meaningful generalization, with success rates remaining in the 0% to 10% range'
2026_evidence_against_the_branch.agentnet_negative_transfer: continuing UI-TARS 7B on 22.5K human trajectories dropped OSWorld from 26.3% to 8-10%. Demonstrations alone did not teach it — they destroyed capability it had.
2026_evidence_against_the_branch.screenshots_or_tools: under one identical harness, the same MCP tools improved a reasoning model +4.0pp and degraded a non-reasoning model -5.9pp. The tools were not the variable.

the_gui_branch.verdict: the GUI branch is not blocked by a missing demonstration. It is blocked by grounding, and 2026 evidence says grounding does not arrive by being shown a thing once.

sentience.why_we_were_doing_it: the stated goal across sixteen rounds
what_2026_science_actually_says: no system has been shown to be conscious, and no agreed test exists that could show it
Butlin et al. indicator framework: current systems satisfy ~3 of 14 indicators
twenty consciousness researchers in Trends in Cognitive Sciences (June 2026) produced credences, not verdicts
Chalmers names six candidate requirements — biology, embodiment, world and self models, recurrent processing, global workspace, unified agency — and puts current LLMs under 10%
Schwitzgebel (Jan 2026) calls the situation an epistemic fog: persistent theory-disagreement means we cannot adjudicate
sentience.the_sharp_point: this is not 'no evidence yet'. The honest form is: the question is undecidable with current science, AND the thing built here is a weaker candidate than the model it sits inside. A sqlite table of argv arrays has none of the six named prerequisites, and does not even have the language model's recurrent depth. Every round spent making the skill index more reliable moved the system AWAY from the sentience question, not toward it. The permanence we proved is the permanence of a file on disk.
sentience.verdict: not sentient. Not close. Not the right direction. Zero evidence, no mechanism, and no test that would settle it.

the_non_obvious_names_audit.claim: we have so many perfect solutions already built, with non-obvious names, somewhere in the repo
the_non_obvious_names_audit.inventory: 16,312 tracked files; 4,410 python modules under canonical/; largest: astra_runtime.py 7,761 lines, goal_compiler.py 7,369, live_brain_route_admission_v1.py 6,467
the_non_obvious_names_audit.what_was_actually_found: the working components are named after what they do — causal_trace_to_skill_compiler_v1, admitted_confinement_execution_v1, read_verb_track_v1. There is no hidden module that does more than its name. The non-obvious names are in the governance and verification trees (3,268 and 2,723 files), which is where the honest record lives.
the_non_obvious_names_audit.verdict: the valuable thing in this repo is not a concealed model. It is a skill compiler that is small enough to verify, plus four rounds of instruments that can prove it wrong — and two occasions (r48, r50) where those instruments caught me.

what_is_real: one demonstration installs one CLI operation
it is permanent and survives restarts
it runs in a new directory on a new file, verified this round
it refuses rather than guesses when it has not been taught
it refuses to compile if trained and tested on the same instance — a real anti-overfitting guard found by accident when my own probe tripped it
every answer carries a source, and that source can be independently replayed and audited
what_is_not_real: that this generalises to all problems
that it composes two learned operations from one sentence
that it finds the object when the goal does not name it
that it turns a computer screenshot into an action, on a machine with no screen
that any of this is on a path to sentience
